headline: 芯, “core, heart, wick”, is traced to Middle Chinese 芯.
トランプ, “playing cards”, is literally English “trump”.
スマート, “smart, stylish, slim”, is the English word “smart” in katakana.
四角い is formed as an -i adjective from 四角 (shikaku, “square, rectangle”).
クラス is the English word “class” in katakana.
入院 is probably from a Middle Chinese compound, literally “enter + institution”.
ポスター is borrowed from English “poster”.
流れ, “stream, current”, is the continuative stem of the verb 流れる (nagareru, “to flow”).
ナイフ is the English word “knife” in katakana.
間違い, “mistake”, is the continuative stem of the verb 間違う (machigau).
テーブル is borrowed from English “table”.
スカート is borrowed from English “skirt”.
ええ, “yes”, is a sound shift from 良い (ei).
ページ is borrowed from English “page”.
酔う took a long road: from Old Japanese wepu to jou, by way of classical 酔ふ.
ビタミン is borrowed from English “vitamin” or German “Vitamin”.
全く is the adverbial form of 全い (mattai).
ステージ covers “stage” and “performance”, and the source traces it to English “stage”.
モノレール is the English word “monorail” in katakana.
宿, “inn, lodging”, is from Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *yanto.
レジャー is borrowed from English “leisure”.
勝ち, “win, victory”, is the continuative stem of the verb 勝つ (katsu, “to win”).
ネックレス is the English word “necklace” in katakana.
承知 is 承 (shō, “agree to”) plus 知 (chi, “know”).
スーツケース is borrowed from English “suitcase”.
好き, “liking, fondness, love”, is the continuative stem of the verb 好く (suku), first cited in the 宇津保物語.
スピーカー is borrowed from English “speaker”.
タイプライター is borrowed from English “typewriter”.
豆, “beans, peas”, is from Old Japanese, in turn from Proto-Japonic *mamay.
サンドイッチ is borrowed from English “sandwich”.
